name: Kernavė Archaeological Site (Cultural Reserve of Kernavė)
description: Kernavė sits in the Neris River valley about 35 km north-west of Vilnius, where people have lived for roughly 10,000 years. Five grassy hill forts rise above the valley, part of a large medieval defence system, and they overlook the remains of a town that served as an early capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. The Teutonic Order destroyed the town in the late 14th century.
